easy.def: To meet something, often by chance.
examples: We encountered a deer.
I encountered a problem.
They encountered a bear.

more.def: To meet someone or something, often without expecting to.
examples: We encountered a deer on the trail.
I encountered a hard word in the book.
The hikers encountered a rushing stream.

easy.def: A meeting that you did not plan.
examples: We had an encounter with a fox.
It was a short encounter.
The encounter was a surprise.

more.def: An unplanned meeting with someone or something.
examples: We had a close encounter with a fox.
It was a brief encounter in the hall.
The encounter surprised them both.

easy.def: To give someone hope to keep trying.
examples: I encourage my friend.
The coach encouraged us.
She encouraged him to try.

more.def: To give someone support and hope so that they keep trying.
examples: The coach encouraged us to keep trying.
She encouraged her friend to enter the contest.
Praise can encourage a child to work hard.

easy.def: Giving you hope or the wish to keep trying.
examples: Her smile was encouraging.
The coach said encouraging words.
That is encouraging news.

more.def: Giving someone hope, confidence or the wish to keep trying.
examples: My teacher wrote an encouraging note on my story.
The doctor had encouraging news about my grandfather's health.
The fans gave the tired runners an encouraging cheer.
The end of the story.
Go to the end of the line.
This is the end.

more.def: The last part of something, or the point where it stops.
examples: We cheered at the end of the movie.
The store is at the end of Maple Street.
Summer ends in the last days of August.
School ends at three.
The show ended.
The rain will end soon.

more.def: To come to a stop, or to bring something to a stop.
examples: The concert ended with a loud round of clapping.
The path ends at a quiet lake.
We ended our picnic when the clouds rolled in.
The story has a happy ending.
The ending was sad.
I liked the ending.

more.def: The last part of a story, movie or something else.
examples: The movie's surprising ending kept us talking.
I did not like the ending of the movie.
The ending of the word is "-ing."
The road seemed endless.
The endless rain fell.
It was an endless line.

more.def: Seeming to go on and on, without an end.
examples: The road seemed endless in the hot sun.
The endless rain made us stay inside.
We waited in an endless line.
I endure the cold.
They endured a long storm.
She endured the pain.

more.def: To stay strong through something hard or painful, or to last a long time.
examples: We endured the cold on the long hike.
The hikers endured a long storm.
The old castle has endured for centuries.

easy.def: Someone who does not like you and wants to hurt you.
examples: The hero beat his enemy.
The cat and the dog are not enemies.
The mouse ran from its enemy.

more.def: A person or group that is against you or wants to harm you.
examples: In the story, the two enemies finally became friends.
Rust is the enemy of old bikes left in the rain.
The two kingdoms had been enemies for a hundred years.

easy.def: What you need to move, play, and grow.
examples: Food gives me energy to run.
The sun gives us energy.
I have no energy today. I need a nap.

more.def: The power that makes things move, work, grow, or give off heat and light.
examples: Solar panels turn energy from the sun into electricity.
The puppy has so much energy that it never sits still.
Wind turbines turn moving air into energy.
Law enforcement keeps us safe.
The enforcement of the rule is strict.
The enforcement began today.

more.def: The act of making sure that people obey a rule or law.
examples: Police officers work in law enforcement.
The enforcement of the speed limit keeps us safe.
The school increased enforcement of the rules.
The story engaged me.
The game engages kids.
She engaged the class.

more.def: To hold someone's attention and interest.
examples: The story engaged the whole class.
A good game engages young players.
She engaged the audience with a funny tale.
They announced their engagement.
The engagement party was fun.
Their engagement lasted a year.

more.def: An agreement between two people to marry each other.
examples: They announced their engagement at dinner.
The engagement lasted a year before the wedding.
My aunt wore her engagement ring.
I have a dinner engagement.
The engagement is at noon.
She has an engagement at three.

more.def: An arrangement to be somewhere at a certain time.
examples: She has a dinner engagement tonight.
The singer had an engagement at the theater.
I cannot come because of a previous engagement.

easy.def: A machine that makes things move.
examples: The car engine is loud.
The boat has an engine.
Start the engine.

more.def: A machine that uses fuel to make a car, boat or plane move.
examples: The engine of the truck roared.
A boat engine pushed us across the bay.
The mechanic fixed the plane's engine.

easy.def: The front part of a train.
examples: The engine pulls the train.
The engine has a whistle.
The train engine is big.

more.def: The part at the front of a train that pulls the other cars.
examples: The engine pulled twenty cars up the hill.
The engine blew its whistle.
The engineer drove the engine slowly.

easy.def: A person who plans and builds things like bridges and machines.
examples: My dad is an engineer.
An engineer designed the bridge.
The engineer drew a plan.

more.def: A person who designs and builds machines, roads, bridges or other things.
examples: An engineer designed the new bridge.
My aunt is an engineer who builds robots.
The engineers tested the model of the airplane.

easy.def: The work of planning and building things like bridges, machines and roads.
examples: Engineering helped build the bridge.
I like engineering.
He studies engineering.

more.def: The use of science and math to plan and build things such as bridges, roads and machines.
examples: Engineering helped build the tall bridge over the river.
She wants to study engineering and design airplanes.
Good engineering makes buildings that stand up in strong winds.
I speak English at school.
This book is in English.
We learn English words.

more.def: The language spoken in the United States, England and many other countries.
examples: She is learning to read in English.
English has many words that came from other languages.
We speak English at home and Spanish with Grandma.
She has an English teacher.
We saw an English castle.
The English countryside is green.

more.def: Belonging to England or its people.
examples: My neighbor has an English bulldog.
The English countryside is full of rolling green hills.
Tea with milk is an English tradition.
I enjoy playing in the snow.
We enjoy the park.
Did you enjoy the movie?

more.def: To get pleasure or happiness from something.
examples: We enjoyed the concert so much that we clapped for five minutes.
My grandfather enjoys working in his garden.
I enjoyed meeting your cousins at the picnic.
An elephant is enormous.
We ate an enormous pizza.
The whale has an enormous tail.

more.def: Much bigger than usual; huge.
examples: An enormous wave crashed over the rocks.
The library has an enormous collection of books.
An enormous tree had fallen across the road.
Do we have enough milk?
I have had enough.
There is enough for all.

more.def: As much as is needed or wanted.
examples: We do not have enough chairs for the whole class.
There is enough time to finish the picture before lunch.
Is the soup hot enough for you?
I ensure the door is locked.
Check to ensure it is safe.
She ensured we had enough food.

more.def: To make certain that something will happen.
examples: I locked the gate to ensure that the dog could not get out.
Check the ice to ensure it is safe.
She packed extra food to ensure we had enough.
Enter the room.
She entered the classroom.
Please enter quietly.

more.def: To go or come into a place.
examples: Please enter through the front door.
The knight entered the great hall.
Visitors enter the museum here.
Enter your name.
She entered the code.
Enter the number.

more.def: To type or put information into a computer or a form.
examples: Enter your password to log in.
She entered her name on the list.
He entered the numbers into the calculator.

easy.def: To join a race or contest.
examples: I will enter the race.
I entered the swim meet.
They entered the art show.

more.def: To take part in a contest.
examples: Over fifty kids entered the art contest.
She entered the spelling bee.
He entered his dog in the pet show.
The clown entertained the kids.
The band entertains the crowd.
She entertains us with jokes.

more.def: To keep people interested and amused, or to welcome guests.
examples: The magician entertained the children with tricks.
We entertained our cousins for the weekend.
The singer entertained the crowd for an hour.
The show was entertaining.
An entertaining story.
The clown is entertaining.

more.def: Holding your attention in an amusing and enjoyable way.
examples: His entertaining stories kept us laughing.
We read an entertaining story about a dog.
The clown was very entertaining.

easy.def: Things that people watch or listen to for fun.
examples: The party had entertainment.
The movie is good entertainment.
The clown was the entertainment.

more.def: Shows, music, games or other things that people enjoy watching or taking part in.
examples: The party had a magician for entertainment.
Movies are a popular form of entertainment.
The band provided the entertainment at the fair.

easy.def: Great excitement about something you like.
examples: She sang with enthusiasm.
We showed enthusiasm for the trip.
His enthusiasm made us smile.

more.def: Strong, eager interest in something you enjoy.
examples: The class sang with great enthusiasm at the school concert.
Her enthusiasm for science made everyone want to join the club.
The coach was pleased by the team's enthusiasm at practice.
I ate the entire pizza.
The entire class sang.
She read the entire book.

more.def: Whole, with nothing left out.
examples: I read the entire book in one day.
The entire class sang happy birthday.
A storm covered the entire town.
I am entirely sure.
The cake was entirely gone.
That is entirely wrong.

more.def: In every part, completely.
examples: I am entirely sure of my answer.
The cake was entirely gone in a minute.
The roof was made entirely of glass.

easy.def: The way in to a place.
examples: The entrance is on the left.
We met at the entrance.
The entrance is wide.

more.def: A door or gate that you use to go into a place.
examples: We waited at the entrance to the zoo.
The cave had a narrow entrance.
The entrance to the school is on the north side.
The entry is at the side.
The entry to the cave was small.
The front entry is open.

more.def: A door or gateway where you go into a place.
examples: The entry to the cave was hidden by bushes.
We waited at the front entry for our friends.
The museum has a large entry.

easy.def: One item in a list or book.
examples: I read the entry in the dictionary.
Write one entry a day.
The entry has a picture.

more.def: One item in a list, diary or dictionary.
examples: Each entry in the dictionary has a definition.
She wrote an entry in her diary.
I read the entry about frogs.

easy.def: A paper cover for a letter.
examples: I put the letter in an envelope.
The envelope has a stamp.
Seal the envelope.

more.def: A flat paper cover that you put a letter or card in.
examples: I put the card in an envelope.
The envelope had her name on the front.
She licked the envelope and sealed it.

easy.def: The land, water, and air around us.
examples: We keep the environment clean.
Trash hurts the environment.
Fish need a clean environment.

more.def: The natural world of land, water, air, plants, and animals around us.
examples: Planting trees is one way to help the environment.
Riding a bike instead of driving is better for the environment.
Oil spills cause great harm to the ocean environment.

easy.def: Having to do with the natural world and keeping it healthy.
examples: We have an environmental club.
The environmental team picks up trash.
Recycling is environmental.

more.def: Having to do with the air, water, land and living things around us.
examples: We have an environmental club at school.
The environmental team cleaned up the river.
Recycling is good for the environment and is an environmental choice.
She felt envy.
He looked at the bike with envy.
Envy is a strong feeling.

more.def: A feeling of wanting something that another person has.
examples: She felt a flash of envy when she saw his new bike.
He looked at the cake with envy.
The sisters were green with envy.
